plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. However, since my value ($35) significantly exceeds the possible maximum value ($20) for any other bidder, I will bid slightly above the maximum possible value to ensure a win. This is because the cost of overpaying (up to $20) is less than the potential profit of winning with a value of $35. I will bid $20.1.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately 2/3 * 20 = $13.33. To maximize profit and win, I should bid just above this. However, my value is $23, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid $13.40 to ensure I win against bids below that.

Since all bidders are rational and know each other are rational, a dominant strategy emerges: bid your true value. This is because any lower bid risks losing the auction when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, resulting in lost potential profit. Bidding higher than your value guarantees a loss, as you'll pay more than the item is worth to you. My value is $21, so I bid $21.
